title: How to Automate Phase 4 in Project P.I.T.T.
description: Concise Phase 4 guide to building a reliable Project P.I.T.T. automation hub, covering a recommended starter lane, panel and mover guidance, and how to chain Shift Scheduler, Trade Terminal, Panel Rack, and x300 Combo.
h1: How to Automate Phase 4 in Project P.I.T.T.
quickAnswer: Begin with a short, visible, recoverable lane (one source, one receiver); use panels as route surfaces and give fans/magnets/pistons/launchers one clear job. In Phase 4 focus on connecting the Shift Scheduler, Trade Terminal, Panel Rack, and x300 Combo while avoiding routing jams and unclear tool roles.

facts.label: First test
facts.value: A short, visible, recoverable lane with one source and one receiver is the recommended starting pattern.

facts.label: Panels
facts.value: Panels can act as route walls and surfaces; a green snap preview indicates a valid snap. Sticky tools help keep contact in place, and fans, magnets, pistons, and launchers should each have one clear job.

facts.label: Phase 4
facts.value: Phase 4 shifts focus to chaining timed and cleanup systems rather than new unlock claims; players should stabilize a short lane, then add timed control and cleanup links. Key tools to prioritize are Shift Scheduler for timed/batch control, Trade Terminal for cleanup, Panel Rack for panel retrieval/spawn behavior, and x300 for the combo attempt. Common blockers include routing jams, unclear tool roles, and poor panel/mover placement.

facts.label: Next tools
facts.value: Establish the natural hub chain: Automation → Shift Scheduler → Trade Terminal → Panel Rack → x300 Combo. Link Trade Terminal for cleanup, Shift Scheduler for timed/batch control, Panel Rack for panel retrieval and spawn behavior, and x300 for the combo attempt.
